name: Oondreeswarar Temple, Poondi (Thiruvenpakkam)
deity: Shiva as Oondreeswarar, who gave the blinded Sundarar a staff to lean on, with the Goddess Minnoli Ammai, the Mother of the lightning
period: A Paadal Petra Sthalam of Thondai Nadu, sung in the Tevaram by Sundarar (8th century)
dynasty: Chola origins; rebuilt at Poondi in the 20th century
summary: On the bank of the Poondi reservoir stands the temple where Shiva gave the blinded saint Sundarar a staff, and the Goddess lit his road as a flash of lightning — the Thiruvenpakkam of the Tevaram, rebuilt stone by stone.

sections.history: Thiruvenpakkam is one of the 276 Paadal Petra Sthalams, a Paadal Petra Sthalam of Thondai Nadu sung by Sundarar in the Tevaram. The temple first stood at Tiruvilamputhur beside the Kosasthalaiyar river, where the Cholas are remembered as its builders. When the Poondi reservoir was planned in the 1940s to bring drinking water to Madras, the old village lay within the land to be flooded; the temple was taken down and raised again on the reservoir's northern bank at Poondi, where it was consecrated in 1968. It stands about 11 km from Tiruvallur, and the shrine keeps its old Tevaram name.
sections.architecture: The rebuilt temple follows the Dravidian plan of its predecessor, with the sanctum of Oondreeswarar and a separate shrine for the Goddess Minnoli Ammai. Two images carry the shrine's story: a figure of Sundarar standing near the Lord, the staff in his left hand and his eyes sightless and sorrowful, and the Nandi facing the sanctum, whose right horn is broken. The quiet waters of the reservoir lie just beyond the temple walls.
sections.legends: The Periya Puranam tells how Sundarar, having broken a vow he had sworn before the Lord, lost the sight of his eyes and set out on a long, groping pilgrimage southward. At Thiruvenpakkam he called out to ask whether the Lord was there; the Lord answered, and placed a staff — an oondrukol — in his hand, giving the shrine its name. Grieving that he was given a staff and not his sight, the saint flung it away, and tradition says it struck and broke the horn of Nandi. Then the Goddess appeared as a flash of lightning to light his road towards Kanchipuram, and so she is Minnoli Ammai.
sections.festivals: Pradosham and Maha Shivaratri are kept with special worship, with Karthigai Deepam and Navaratri for the Goddess. The days sacred to Sundarar are remembered here with particular feeling; confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: The temple is a quiet place beside the great reservoir, and its story is one of the most human in the Tevaram: a saint who had lost his sight, a staff given in compassion, and a light to walk by. Devotees stand before the sorrowing image of Sundarar and the broken-horned Nandi, and remember the grace that met the saint in his darkness.

visit.timings: Open daily in morning and evening sessions with a midday closure, as at most village temples. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left outside before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is not permitted inside the sanctum; in the outer areas, ask the temple staff before taking pictures, especially of rituals.
visit.gettingThere: The temple stands at Poondi on the northern bank of the Poondi reservoir, about 11 km from Tiruvallur by road. Tiruvallur is a station on the Chennai–Arakkonam suburban line with buses and autos onward to Poondi; Chennai International Airport is the nearest airport.
